[[Category: Cherry Fork Cemetery, Cherry Fork, Ohio]] 

== Biography ==
Robert was born in 1848. He was the son of [[Glasgow-17|Stewart Glasgow]] and [[Askren-120|Elizabeth Askren]].  He passed away in 1871. 
== Research Notes ==
=== Peoria family and parentage ===

The separately assessed mother [[Askren-120]] is confidently assessed at 96%: first individual maternal rating from the explicit 1880 mother–son wording. The parent ratings share their identity evidence.


The original 1880 Peoria biography of [[Glasgow-17|Stewart Glasgow]] explicitly names [[Glasgow-1923|Huston]] as a child of Stewart and his first wife [[Askren-120|Elizabeth Askren]]. The distinctive parental couple identifies the existing Robert Houston [[Glasgow-1923]], already represented by Faris p. 63 and the held 1850/1870 census references. The 25 October 1925 interview independently recalls [[Glasgow-17|Stuart]]’s son [[Glasgow-1923|Huston]] dying unmarried at his uncle [[Glasgow-16|Finley]]’s home, connecting the Ohio and Peoria family accounts. This supplies explicit father–son wording absent from the previously held citation summaries.<ref>The History of Peoria County, Illinois (Chicago: Johnson & Company, 1880), pp. 791–792, Stewart Glasgow sketch. Modern library transcription of a dated interview, visually inspected; not a manuscript facsimile. Names Stuart’s son Huston and uncle Finley, but his reported age 26 conflicts with the county sketch and held dates.</ref>

The existing father is confidently assessed at 96%. 96% is a subjective confident assessment of the complete father–child identity. Huston is the source form; Robert Houston is the compatible profile. The printed biography is contemporary with the surviving father but retrospective about his deceased son, and its informant is unnamed. The later recollection is not a contemporary death entry. The 1880 sketch prints Stewart’s birth as 23 April 1823, versus the retained 13 April field. It says Huston died aged 24; the 1925 recollection says 26, while the retained 23 August 1848–15 October 1871 dates imply 23. The 1925 account’s death “2 or 3 years ago” also conflicts with Stewart’s retained 1904 death, and its “second wife” Edith omits Hadassah. The matching Peoria residence, first wife and son identify the family despite these specific errors; none supplies authority to overwrite the dates. Inspect Faris p. 63 and original death/marriage records to resolve them.


=== Earlier father review, 22 October 2026 — superseded below ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-17]] is assessed at 88% (probable). Robert’s held account names Stewart Glasgow and Elizabeth Askren and cites Faris p 63 with 1850/1870 censuses. The 1848 birth fits Stewart’s first family, but no literal parental field from those records is held.

Confidence concerns this recorded child and the selected father as identified by the held family evidence; maternity and the father’s upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Inspect 1850 household and Faris p 63 source notes.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1923 US Federal Census (1850, 1870),]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
